findings.problem: The default npm test command does not execute tests/electron-runtime.test.mjs, so the desktop file-routing and no-server startup contract can regress while the standard test entrypoint remains green.
findings.proposed_fix: Include the focused Electron runtime test in npm test, or make npm test delegate to both the existing ERD tests and npm run test:electron.

findings.problem: The Electron window retains secure renderer defaults but has no explicit navigation or new-window policy, even though the shared renderer contains external links and window.open calls.
findings.proposed_fix: Add will-navigate and setWindowOpenHandler policies that deny unexpected Electron navigation/windows and route explicitly allowlisted external URLs through the OS browser.

findings.problem: The successful user-smoke result is generated by the Vite web-baseline harness on 127.0.0.1 and therefore does not demonstrate a real Electron GUI launch or visible editor from bundled file URLs.
findings.proposed_fix: Add separate Electron smoke evidence that launches the built desktop runtime without Vite or a loopback server and verifies the visible editor route, while retaining this artifact only as web-preservation evidence.

findings.problem: Desktop actions still call window.open with absolute BrowserRouter paths such as /editor and /bug-report; from file:///.../index.html#/editor these resolve to filesystem URLs rather than HashRouter routes.
findings.proposed_fix: Introduce a small environment-aware route-opening helper that emits hash URLs for file-based desktop windows and ordinary paths for the web, and cover the new-window editor and bug-report actions in the focused routing test.

checks_run.summary: Compiled scripts/check_web_smoke.py successfully with no Python syntax errors.
Both default ERD test files passed: 2 tests, 0 failures.
ESLint completed with no warnings or errors.
The ordinary Vite web build completed after transforming 2,648 modules; only dependency eval and chunk-size warnings were reported.
The focused Electron suite built all runtime artifacts and passed its file routing, local asset, no-server, web-router preservation, and security-default assertions.

file_url_routing_correctness.justification: loadFile supplies #/editor and the renderer selects HashRouter for file: documents, so initial /editor startup is correct; absolute-path window.open actions remain incompatible with file-based hash routing.

offline_startup_without_web_server.justification: The built-main harness proves local loadFile startup and local relative assets without server modules or localhost asset URLs; a real Electron GUI smoke is still absent.

web_browserrouter_preservation.justification: Non-file documents still use BrowserRouter, npm run build passes, and the normal web output retains root-relative asset URLs.

security_regressions.justification: No routing-repair regression was found: isolation, sandboxing, disabled Node integration, and the narrow preload remain intact; explicit navigation and new-window controls are a retained hardening gap.

test_integration.justification: The focused suite is meaningful and passes, but it remains outside the default npm test entrypoint.

scope_control.justification: The observable repair is limited to the Electron load target, protocol-gated router choice, and focused test coverage; no unjustified feature or dependency expansion was found.
